newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rio's gays march for tolerance and right to marry.
newsitem.headline: Rio's gays march for tolerance and right to marry.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro's gay and lesbian community came out in full force on Sunday to stage its third annual Lesbian and Gay Pride march along Rio's world famous Copacabana beach.

Under cloudy skies, crowds lined the beachfront promenade to take in the colourful two-hour spectacle and watch the more than 1,000 gays and lesbians, including a lesbian couple in full wedding gear, wave their banners to the sound of Afro-Brazilian drums.

"This march is a matter of citizenship, greater tolerance and harmony," said Raimundo Pereira, one of the organisers of gay rights group Atoba. "Homosexuality is not a sickness or an abnormality, but just another sexual preference."
Transvestites with 10-inch (25 cm) platform shoes, exotic costumes and thick makeup charmed the crowds, but mock lesbian brides dressed in long white wedding gowns stole the show.

Accompanied by their sexy transvestite bridesmaids in neon green and orange wigs, short black dresses and fishnet stockings, the lesbian couple staged a mock wedding at the end of the march to express support for gay and lesbian marriages.
"We want to make people more sensitive to our needs and desires," said lesbian bride Sarandah Vilas Boas as tears rolled down her face after the ceremony. "We all have a right to be happy."

A law which would allow gays and lesbians to be married in civil ceremonies is currently under discussion in Brazil's lower house of Congress, but deputies have come under strong pressures from church leaders not to vote in favour of the legislation.

Deputy Fernando Gabeira, who took part in the march, said approval of the law would not only enable gays and lesbians to enjoy the same legal rights as heterosexual couples, but it would also help diminish prejudice and aggression against homosexuals.
He said one homosexual was killed every three days in Brazil, often in knife attacks.
